guide.summary: Temples, tombs, a sound-and-light show and a balloon operator on both banks of Luxor, with breakfast spots, dinners and bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: The ministry's ticket site lists Karnak Temple, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut as open all days, but Karnak's last entry is 04:00 pm in every season, so visit it before Luxor Temple, where last entry is 07:00 pm.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The ministry's ticket site, egymonuments.com, lists Karnak Temple, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut as open all days. None of the places in this guide publishes a weekly closing day.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Karnak Temple, Luxor Temple and the Temple of Hatshepsut can be booked on egymonuments.com, which lists adult tickets for foreign visitors at EGP 600, EGP 500 and EGP 440; the Valley of the Kings is listed at EGP 750. The Karnak Sound and Light Show sells tickets online at $20, and its page warns that dates are subject to change.

toolkit.label: Last entry and tables
toolkit.copy: The ticket site asks you to arrive at least one hour before a site's closing time; Karnak's last entry is 04:00 pm, while the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut take last entry at 05:00 pm in summer and 04:00 pm in winter. Al-Sahaby Lane Restaurant takes table requests online and confirms a table only after its team contacts you.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: At the ministry sites, students must show a valid ID and be 24 or under, children below 6 enter free, and photography with a mobile phone is free of charge. The Karnak Sound and Light Show charges $11 for children aged 6 to 12, and its second evening show runs only with at least five foreign visitors.

guide.dek: Do Karnak first, since its last entry is 04:00 pm, and save Luxor Temple and the sound-and-light show for the evening.
intro: Luxor's headline sights are run by Egypt's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, and its online ticket site, egymonuments.com, lists Karnak Temple, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut as open all days. None of the places checked here publishes a weekly closing day. The same site asks you to arrive at least one hour before a site's closing time, to keep your ticket with you, and notes that photography with a mobile phone is free of charge.

On the east bank, the ticket site lists Karnak Temple from 06:00 with last entry at 04:00 pm in every season, and its EGP 600 adult ticket for foreign visitors also covers the Open Museum at Karnak. Luxor Temple, about three kilometres south of Karnak according to the ministry, has the latest last entry of the four, 07:00 pm. In the evening, Misr Company for Sound, Light and Tourism Development lists a 19:00 English show at Karnak, with a second show at 20:00 that needs at least five foreign visitors.

Across the river, the ministry places the Valley of the Kings on the west side of the Nile and the Temple of Hatshepsut at Deir al-Bahari, directly across from Karnak. The ticket site gives both a 06:00 opening, with last entry at 05:00 pm in summer and 04:00 pm in winter and Ramadan; adult tickets for foreign visitors are EGP 750 and EGP 440. If you want to see the west bank from above first, Sindbad Balloons lists daily, year-round flights with sunrise and morning departures, and offers hotel pickup in Luxor when you book.

For meals, Al-Sahaby Lane Restaurant at the Nefertiti Hotel serves an open buffet breakfast daily from 7:00 to 10:00 on its rooftop and takes table requests through an online form. On the west bank, Al Moudira's Ottoman Hall serves a fusion dinner menu, The Courtyard covers breakfast and coffee, and The Eastern Bar handles aperitivo. Back on the east bank, the Steigenberger Resort Achti lists Sukkareya Lobby Bar & Terrace from 09:00 to 01:00 and Nino's Restaurant for Italian dinners from 18:00 to 22:00.
summaryCards: Start at Karnak Temple, where the ministry's ticket site sets last entry at 04:00 pm every day, and leave Luxor Temple for later, as it admits visitors until 07:00 pm.
Take the 7:00 to 10:00 buffet breakfast on the rooftop at Al-Sahaby Lane Restaurant, then cross to the Temple of Hatshepsut, which opens at 06:00.
None of these places publishes a weekly closing day, but the ministry asks you to arrive at least one hour before closing, and students need a valid ID showing they are 24 or under.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and show details do not guarantee availability. Monument hours are taken from the ministry's ticket site (egymonuments.com), which carries no date; the ministry's information pages on egymonuments.gov.eg (footer dated 2019) list different closing times, for example Karnak to 05:00 PM and Luxor Temple to 08:00 PM, so check at the ticket office. Monument locations are published only as descriptions (east or west bank, distance from Karnak), not street addresses. The Al Moudira venues publish no hours, Al-Sahaby Lane publishes only breakfast hours, Sindbad Balloons does not name its launch site, and the Nile Valley Hotel gives a location rather than a street address. Sofitel Winter Palace (Accor pages gone or redirected), Hilton Luxor (403), Sofra Restaurant & Café and Hod Hod Soliman (domains did not resolve) could not be read; the Luxor Museum, Mummification Museum, Ramesseum and Medinet Habu were left out because no official page read gives their exact location. No dedicated bakery or coffee shop with an official website was found; those lists rely on hotel restaurant menus.
